relevance.rationale: Join CORRECT (arXiv:math/0209324v1, 'Cyclotomic completions of polynomial rings', Habiro, matching the registered entry's title, DOI and URL). Widely and accurately cited: ten-plus Lean sites including mass-theory/qz-bicompletion.lean:20, habiro-expansion-atomic.lean:23,121, z-habiro-ring.lean:20, habiro-ring.lean:14,27,34, appendix-qvalues/qbeta-ck-truncation-canonical.lean:81, lean/QOU/MassEndomorphism/ZHabiroCauchy.lean:241,401, plus mass-theory/quantum-dilog-convergence.ts:14. Load-bearing and correctly matched to the source: the abstract of this document defines exactly the object the Lean sites name - the completion Z[q]_N = lim_n Z[q]/((1-q)(1-q^2)...(1-q^n)) - and proves the two facts the corpus leans on, that an element of Z[q]_N is determined by its power-series expansion at each root of unity and by its values at the roots of unity ('holomorphic functions on the set of roots of unity'), along with the generalisation to R[q] completions at products of cyclotomic polynomials. The registry note correctly separates this key from habiro2000 and habiro2002.

keyResults.statement: Every element of Z[q]_N is uniquely determined by its power-series expansion in q - zeta at each root of unity zeta, and equally by its values at the roots of unity.
keyResults.useForFolio: This is the determinacy property the Habiro-ring blocks rely on when they treat a Habiro element as pinned by its root-of-unity data; it is the fibre-level statement behind the AGENTS.md framing that a c_k closure must be sought as a Habiro element rather than a real function of q_0.
